description.value: This cross-sectional multimodal structural neuroimaging study investigated differences in white matter integrity, gray matter volume, and cortical thickness between poly-drug use disordered patients and healthy controls.

spans.text: This study investigated alterations in brain structure in an unprecedented large sample of PUD patients compared to controls from the general population.

description.value: Diffusion data were visually inspected, denoised with MRtrix dwidenoise, corrected for geometric distortion and eddy-current effects using FSL topup and eddy or eddy_correct, coregistered to the structural image with SPM12, segmented into five tissue classes, used to estimate tissue-specific response functions, and processed with multitissue constrained spherical deconvolution to compute fiber orientation distributions. Whole-brain tractography was generated with 5 million tracks and reduced to 1 million using SIFT to reduce tractogram biases.

description.value: T1-weighted structural scans were processed with CAT12 in SPM12. For voxel-based morphometry, scans were visually checked, segmented, modulated, normalized to MNI space at 1.5 mm, assessed for sample homogeneity, and used to estimate total intracranial volume before 8 mm Gaussian smoothing. Cortical thickness was extracted with CAT12 using tissue segmentation and a projection-based algorithm, followed by 15 mm surface smoothing.
